description: Several entry points in this slice were inferred from confirmed child URLs rather than fetched directly: the Věstník year-index hub, the informační povinnosti parent hub, and the ČNB kalendář parent. The dohledový benchmark PDF path pattern was likewise generalised from four observed files.

ČNB is the rule-maker for implementing acts, but primary statutes (zákon o bankách 21/1992 Sb., zákon o platebním styku 370/2017 Sb., zákon o ČNB 6/1993 Sb.) originate with Ministerstvo financí / Ministerstvo spravedlnosti and are authentically published in the Sbírka zákonů (e-Sbírka / Zákony pro lidi). This cell deliberately does not cover them.

A large share of what binds CZ banks and PSPs originates at EBA/ESMA/EIOPA, the ECB/SSM and the EU institutions; ČNB's role is often to declare compliance and set application dates. This slice captures only the ČNB-side transmission notices.

Year-index pages for Věstník ČNB were confirmed as far back as 1998, but the completeness, format consistency, and OCR-readability of older částky (scanned vs digital-native PDFs) were not tested in this pass.

A definitive inventory of the ČNB soft-law instrument types was not completed. Confirmed: vyhláška, opatření obecné povahy, úřední sdělení, dohledový benchmark, stanovisko (RS series), sdělení o obecných pokynech. Not yet confirmed as separate tracked families: 'otázky a odpovědi' / FAQ pages, metodické listy, and dohledové priority statements.

ČNB's robots.txt, terms of use, and any stated reuse/licensing conditions for its published documents were not read in this pass. Collection permissibility was assumed from the public-sector, mandatory-publication character of the material.

Parliamentary and Sbírka-zákonů stages were not scouted in this pass: PSP ČR sněmovní tisky, Senát, and the e-Sbírka / Sbírka zákonů a mezinárodních smluv, which carry the definitive effective dates and transitional provisions once a consultation closes.
Exact RSS/Atom endpoint URLs behind the ČNB RSS directory were not enumerated, so the cheapest low-latency ingest path is described but not yet concretely specified.

AML/CFT (FAÚ – Finanční analytický úřad) and cyber/operational-resilience (NÚKIB, ZKB implementing decrees, DORA) consultation and deadline streams touch banks and payment firms but sit outside ČNB and were only glimpsed via a NÚKIB result.

No archival/decay strategy was established for closed consultations — ČNB and MF pages reorganise and consultation deadlines decay fast, so historic comment windows and their vypořádání may vanish from the live index.

Non-bank payment institutions and electronic money institutions (platební instituce / instituce elektronických peněz) are under-covered relative to banks. Only GoPay, Comgate and Citfin were reached; the full ČNB-licensed population was not enumerated.

Client-facing 'Oznámení' documents (KB-style 'Oznámení o provádění platebního styku', cut-off times, payment-execution notices) were only touched incidentally, yet they are where operational effects of payments law land.

Regulatory themes beyond PSD2/SEPA/instant payments — DORA operational-resilience notices, AML/KYC client-information updates, and PSD3/PSR readiness statements — were not surfaced from regulated-entity publishers in this run.
T&C and API notices are typically replaced in place; historical versions (needed to date when a rule actually arrived) are often not retained by the publisher.

Several portal URLs in this slice come from a community index that self-describes updates as sporadic (e.g. Equa bank and Sberbank CZ entries reference institutions that have since merged or exited the CZ market).
Broadcast and public-service TV coverage (ČT24 / Události v regionech, ceskatelevize.cz) and the ČTK wire (ceskenoviny.cz) were not scouted in this pass, though both carry same-day regulatory news.
No archival/full-text route identified for paywalled Czech business press.
Consultation-stage coverage (připomínkové řízení, veřejná konzultace) is thinly represented among media sources; media mostly report after drafts are public.
No source in this slice was fetched directly; all evidence is from search-result metadata and snippets.
The concrete e-Sbírka API base URL, endpoint list and bulk-download distribution URLs were not pinned down in this pass — only the announcement page and the operator were identified.
This slice covers the government (ODok/VeKLEP) and Chamber of Deputies stages but did not map Senát PČR document/open-data channels, which carry a distinct set of deadlines.
EUR-Lex / EU Official Journal Czech-language corpus and the CZ transposition notification records (which drive most CZ banking/payments deadlines) were out of scope of this pass.
Paywalled professional corpora (ASPI/Wolters Kluwer, Beck-online, CODEXIS) were not assessed; they carry richer amendment metadata and commentary but under restrictive licences.
No baseline inventory yet exists of which ČNB/MF/Vláda legacy URLs (cnb.cz, mfcr.cz, vlada.cz, odok.cz) have already migrated to .gov.cz and which redirect versus 404.
The Collection of International Treaties (Sbírka mezinárodních smluv) strand within e-Sbírka was not separately examined, though it matters for cross-border supervisory arrangements.

EU-level reciprocity and buffer registers (ESRB national measures database, EBA CCyB register, ESRB recommendations on reciprocation) were not pinned down, so the cell currently has only the national side of dated macroprudential obligations.

Coverage skews to banking/credit. Payments-specific supervisory outputs (payment institutions, e-money institutions, PSD2/PSD3-related supervisory expectations, DORA oversight) were not separately enumerated even though the run scope is sector=both.

The depth of the online archive for the supervisory report and for the opatření obecné povahy series was inferred from search results, not enumerated. Earliest available year and any gaps are unknown.

English mirrors clearly exist for the CCyB provisions, financial stability reports and Bank Board decisions, but parity was not confirmed for the Dohledová úřední sdělení a benchmarky series or the supervisory strategy page — these may be Czech-only.

Sanction and enforcement decision outputs (pravomocná rozhodnutí, sankční řízení) are referenced from the Výkon dohledu hub via a dedicated application but were not enumerated as a source in this pass.

Individual CZ bank and PSP career portals (ČSOB, Komerční banka, Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank, MONETA, Air Bank, Fio, ČSOB PS, Comgate, ThePay, Global Payments CZ) were not enumerated; only one bank career page was captured.

LinkedIn (company pages, LinkedIn Events, and posts by CZ compliance officers and RegTech vendors) is the most active informal channel for seminar/webinar announcements but was not collected due to access and ToS constraints.
Slovak-language material was not searched, although the flagship payments conference is explicitly ČR & SR and many CZ obligations are discussed jointly with SK counterparts.

No source yet captured for training/certification bodies in AML and payments (e.g. ICT/AML certification providers, Czech Institute of Internal Auditors, ACAMS CZ chapter) whose curriculum changes track new obligations.
No structured way yet to convert agenda/job-ad text into a dated obligation register; sources are catalogued but the deadline-extraction method is unspecified.
The JERRS web application's query URL structure (roles, list codes, pagination, export options) was not mapped; only the login/entry URLs are known.

Passporting notifications — foreign payment institutions, e-money institutions and banks notified to operate in CZ under freedom of services/establishment, and CZ entities passporting out — were not located as a distinct ČNB list in this pass.

Non-ČNB Czech registers that complement the supervisory ones — obchodní rejstřík / justice.cz, ARES, evidence skutečných majitelů (UBO register), and the Finanční analytický úřad (FAÚ) AML side — were out of this cell's scope but are needed to resolve entity identity and ownership behind register entries.
Register snapshots are current-state only; JERRS does not obviously expose historical states beyond the vznik/zánik query, and open-data CSVs are overwritten.
The English mirror of ČNB pages exists but was only spot-checked; whether the EN site carries the same register links and the same freshness as the CS site is unconfirmed.

Comment-procedure OUTPUT (vypořádání připomínek — who objected and how MF resolved it) was not located as a separately monitorable feed; it is normally an annex inside the government-meeting material rather than an indexed document.

Industry comment bodies specific to banking/payments (Česká bankovní asociace, ČLFA, ČNB as připomínkové místo, Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů) were not scouted in this cell — only the cross-sector Hospodářská komora was found.
No structured alerting mechanism (RSS/Atom/email subscription) was confirmed for any of the primary state sources; monitoring design currently assumes polling.
No confirmed crosswalk between the three identifier systems in this pipeline: eKLEP PID (KORNxxxxxxx), sněmovní tisk number + volební období, and the final Sbírka zákonů number.

Deposit insurance / resolution (zákon o bankách, Garanční systém finančního trhu), AML (zákon č. 253/2008 Sb., new Finanční analytický úřad package spotted in HK ČR listings) and the 'digitalizace finančního trhu' (DORA/MiCA) vehicle were only touched incidentally.

ESMA and EIOPA were not scouted in this pass even though they co-issue guidelines that ČNB adopts via the same 'Sdělení ČNB' mechanism (relevant to MiCA on the ESMA side, and to bancassurance distribution).

EU legislative-process trackers (EP Legislative Observatory / OEIL, Council public register, Interinstitutional file numbers) were not scouted. These carry trilogue documents and adoption dates months before EUR-Lex publication.

Industry scheme-level rulebooks (European Payments Council SCT Inst rulebook, Verification of Payee scheme rules) were not scouted. IPR compliance for CZ banks is executed through EPC scheme deadlines, not only through the Regulation's own dates.
Czech-language coverage is strong for national adoption artefacts (ČNB, MF, FAÚ, ISAP) but thin for EU-origin consultation and pre-legislative material, which is English-only in practice.

The Czech national statute-book layer (Sbírka zákonů / e-Sbírka, zákon č. 31/2025 Sb. and 32/2025 Sb.) was identified only indirectly through ČNB and MF pages, not scouted as a source in its own right.

Official legislative pipeline sources are not yet pinned: e-Sbírka (esbirka.cz / sbirka.gov.cz) for authoritative consolidated AMLZ text and effective dates, eKLEP/VeKLEP for inter-ministerial comment procedure on AML bills, and psp.cz for parliamentary passage of AMLZ novely.

EU-level sanctions list feeds that Czech obliged entities must screen against (EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List / FSD, EU Sanctions Map, UN Security Council consolidated list) were referenced indirectly via FAÚ 'informační zdroje' but not individually catalogued with verified URLs.

Co-supervisors and adjacent AML authorities for specific obliged-entity classes were not covered: Celní správa ČR (gambling sector, co-author of MP č. 6), Česká obchodní inspekce, professional chambers (ČAK for lawyers, notarial and auditor chambers), and the Evidence skutečných majitelů register operated by the courts.

Version history of metodické pokyny is not preserved anywhere obvious: FAÚ replaces PDFs at stable-looking asset paths and different filename patterns coexist (/assets/cs/cmsmedia/... vs /files/...), so silent re-issues can be missed.
English coverage on fau.gov.cz is partial and lags the Czech tree (only selected guidelines such as MP č. 9 exist in EN); several sanctions and stanoviska pages appear cs-only.
No confirmed URL for the ÚOOÚ úřední deska (official notice board) or a structured register of its administrative decisions/fines was captured.
NÚKIB legislative sub-pages (vyhlášky, metodiky, podpůrné materiály) and the úřední deska were seen only as menu labels, not as confirmed deep URLs.

Adjacent actors not yet scouted in this cell: ČTÚ (electronic communications, relevant to SMS/2FA and mobile payments), MPO as ČOI's parent and consumer-law legislator, EDPB/EDPS Czech contributions, and the Sbírka zákonů / e-Sbírka as the authoritative promulgation source.
Consumer NGOs that generate conduct pressure and complaint data (dTest, SOS - Asociace beyond its supervisor map) were not individually scouted.

Authority-level public consultations (ÚOOÚ methodological consultations, NÚKIB draft-decree comment rounds) were only reached indirectly via ODok/VeKLEP; no authority-hosted consultation page was confirmed.
Member circulars — one of the four artefact types named in this cell — are behind member logins at SBK and ČLFA and are not surfaced at all by ČBA or ČEFTAS.
czech-ba.cz could not be fetched (403) and cbamonitor.cz was catalogued from a navigation link only, without inspecting its publication index. Both may hold substantial A3 material.

The cell seed list omits several associations that ČNB itself recognises and that touch payments/banking regulation: Asociace družstevních záložen (ADZ, credit unions), Asociace penzijních společností ČR (APS ČR), Česká asociace společností finančního poradenství a zprostředkování (ČASF), Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP), plus Česká kryptoměnová asociace (ČKMA) and the Hospodářská komora as a formal comment place.

ODOK/VeKLEP is identified as the single highest-value place to find dated, itemised association comments, but no reliable way to enumerate materials by respondent or by financial-market topic was established in this pass — only two example material IDs were observed.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin and mostly EU-hosted (EBA responses, EFAMA relays, /en mirrors that are shallower than the cs originals). ČEFTAS is the only cell actor with a substantive English site.
An RSS option was observed on AKAT document listings, but no systematic check for RSS/Atom/iCal feeds was performed across cbaonline.cz, clfa.cz, bankovnikarty.cz or czechfintech.cz.
Named-target firms PRK Partners, Kinstellar and A&O Shearman were confirmed as actors but their actual publication indexes (news/insights URLs) were not opened and their cadence is unknown.

Local-language coverage was achieved for Czech domestic firms and the Big Four (queries in cs), but the international Prague offices were only searched in English because no Czech-language alert vocabulary for them was observed on the sites reached.

Consultations (ČNB and MFČR consultation responses authored by advisers, adviser commentary on draft Czech implementing legislation) are thinly covered by the sources found — adviser output skews to post-adoption explainers.

Payments/PSD3-PSR adviser coverage in CZ was found mostly via epravo.cz articles and non-law vendors (Monet+, Aisa International); no dedicated CZ law-firm payments-regulation channel beyond FINREG PARTNERS was identified.
Historical depth of the periodic series was only spot-checked (Schönherr/epravo back to 2021, EY back to 2023); no archive index was enumerated.

Only one CZ acquirer merchant manual (ČSOB) was located. The other major CZ acquirers/PSPs — KB/Worldline, Česká spořitelna/Global Payments, Fio, Raiffeisenbank, ComGate, GoPay, Besteron, Monri/Twisto — were not individually scouted for their scheme-mandate documentation.

CERTIS technical annexes (technické přílohy) are referenced as part of the Rules but were not individually enumerated; they carry the implementation-level dated obligations for participants' message formats and cut-off times.

Adjacent scheme rulebooks binding CZ actors were not covered in this pass: SEPA Direct Debit (Core/B2B), SEPA Request-to-Pay (SRTP), SPAA, OCT Inst, and card-adjacent standards (PCI DSS/PCI PIN, EMVCo, nexo/Berlin Group for terminal estates).
Czech-language coverage is strong for CERTIS, COBS and Bank iD but essentially absent for EPC rulebooks; no Czech translation or ČBA-issued CZ commentary on EPC rulebook deadlines was located.
No URL in this slice was fetched and confirmed reachable; all entries derive from search-result metadata and snippets.
